plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 27: Biomolecules: Lipids
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets a three-dimensional rendering of a lipid bilayer beside the flat structural formula of the molecule that builds it. On the left, a slab of membrane is drawn in perspective with a stepped cutaway at one corner: rows of small green spheres tile the top and bottom faces, and the interior between them is packed with pale tan wavy strands that meet tip to tip along the slab's midplane, so the two leaflets face each other tails inward. On the right, a glycerophospholipid is drawn with a vertical glycerol backbone reading CH2, CH, CH2 from top to bottom. The topmost branch is printed in green and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+, tagged by a green arrow labeled "Ionic head". The two lower branches each run through O-C(=O) into a long tan ribbon of the same shade and waviness as the strands filling the slab, and a magenta label "Nonpolar tails" sends two arrows to their free ends. Matching the green and tan across the two halves lets the reader place each region of the drawn molecule at its position in the assembled sheet. The pairing accounts for how a long nonpolar tail bound to a polar ionic head drives aggregation into a bilayer that keeps hydrocarbon away from water.

elements: LEFT slab: top-leaflet grid of green ionic-head spheres tiling the upper face
LEFT slab: bottom-leaflet grid of green ionic-head spheres tiling the lower face
LEFT slab: upper-leaflet pale-tan wavy tail strands hanging downward from the top heads
LEFT slab: lower-leaflet pale-tan wavy tail strands rising upward from the bottom heads
LEFT slab: midplane seam where the two tail sets meet tip-to-tip
LEFT slab: stepped cutaway notch at the front-top-left corner exposing the interior strands
LEFT slab: pale pink-tan membrane body side faces
RIGHT molecule: vertical glycerol backbone line with stacked labels CH2 (top), CH (middle), CH2 (bottom)
RIGHT molecule: top green branch CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+ with double-bonded O and O- on phosphorus
RIGHT molecule: green arrow and 'Ionic head' text label pointing at the phosphate-choline group
RIGHT molecule: two ester linkages O-C(=O) branching from CH and bottom CH2
RIGHT molecule: two long pale-tan wavy ribbon tails extending rightward from the esters
RIGHT molecule: magenta 'Nonpolar tails' text with two arrows to the free ends of the ribbons
RIGHT molecule: glycerol-linker region (backbone + ester oxygens) as a distinct highlightable zone

interactions.label: Highlight region
interactions.teaches: Selecting a region (by stepping the buttons or clicking the matching spheres / backbone / strands in the scene) glows that part in BOTH the structural formula and the bilayer slab, so the learner sees exactly where the polar head, the linker, and the hydrophobic tails sit inside the assembled membrane

interactions.label: Mapping view
interactions.teaches: Switches which half carries the named callout labels while the matching region glows on the other half, reinforcing the one-to-one correspondence between a single glycerophospholipid's zones and its position in the bilayer

interactions.label: Cutaway depth
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the slice plane through the slab peels away successive layers — first the outer green heads, then the tan tails, finally revealing the midplane tail-to-tail contact — making the outside-polar / inside-nonpolar organization across the membrane thickness directly visible

demo_steps.title: Ionic head maps to the surfaces
demo_steps.narration: With the molecule in focus, the green phosphate-choline head is highlighted; the same green glow appears on the sphere layers capping both faces of the slab, showing the polar heads face the aqueous exterior.

demo_steps.title: Nonpolar tails map to the core
demo_steps.narration: Selecting the tan tails highlights the two wavy ribbons in the formula and the strand-packed interior of the slab, showing the hydrophobic chains are buried away from water.

demo_steps.title: Read the mapping from the assembly
demo_steps.narration: Switching to Assembly view puts the named labels on the slab while the glycerol-linker zone glows in the formula, confirming the ester/backbone band sits at the head-tail interface.

demo_steps.title: Slice to the midplane
demo_steps.narration: Pushing the cutaway to full depth removes the near leaflet's heads and tails, exposing the seam where the two tail sets meet tip-to-tip at the membrane midplane.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Two side-by-side groups. LEFT bilayer slab centered near world x=-3: overall ~4 (X, screen-right width) x 2 (Y, thickness) x 2.5 (Z, receding depth). Top-leaflet head spheres at y=+1, bottom at y=-1, sphere radius ~0.13, arranged ~8 columns (X) x 5 rows (Z) per face as an InstancedMesh. Tan tail strands are wavy tubes/lines spanning y from +/-1 toward the y=0 midplane where the two leaflets meet tip-to-tip. A stepped cutaway notch (~1.5 X x 1 Y x 1.2 Z) is removed from the front-top-left corner to expose interior strands. Membrane body side faces pale pink-tan #d8b3a3. RIGHT molecule on a camera-facing flat group centered near world x=+3.5: vertical glycerol backbone at local x=0 from y=+1.2 (top CH2) through y=0 (CH) to y=-1.2 (bottom CH2); top green branch (#159e7c) runs +X as CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+; two ester O-C(=O) groups at y=0 and y=-1.2 each feed a long tan (#cf9f8a) wavy ribbon extending +X to ~+2.2; green 'Ionic head' arrow/label above the phosphate, magenta (#d6338f) 'Nonpolar tails' label with two arrows at the ribbon free ends. Head spheres green #3ec9a7. Highlight = emissive/opacity boost on the selected group plus dimming of the other two; the same region id drives both halves.
interactionPlan.notes: Three.js: render head spheres as an InstancedMesh for performance; render tails as TubeGeometry along a sine-perturbed path (or fat lines) so they read as wavy strands. Build the structural formula from Line segments plus canvas-texture text sprites on a group that is oriented to face the camera (billboarded) so the formula stays legible at the fixed three-quarter view. Implement the cutaway slider by hiding head-sphere instances and tail tubes whose Z (or distance from the near face) falls within the sliced band, and clip the membrane body with a THREE.Plane clipping plane at the slice position; at depth=1 also reveal the midplane seam line. Wire a raycaster so clicking a sphere / backbone segment / strand sets the highlightRegion state, keeping the click gesture and the explicit stepper in sync. No orbit control — camera is fixed so the flat formula plane is never skewed.

authoredContext:
Phospholipids are found widely in both plant and animal tissues and make up approximately 50% to 60% of cell membranes. Because they are like soaps in having a long, nonpolar hydrocarbon tail bound to a polar ionic head, phospholipids in the cell membrane organize into a lipid bilayer about 5.0 nm (50 Å) thick. As shown in the figure, the nonpolar tails aggregate in the center of the bilayer in much the same way that soap tails aggregate in the center of a micelle. This bilayer serves as an effective barrier to the passage of water, ions, and other components into and out of cells.

Aggregation of glycerophospholipids into the lipid bilayer that composes cell membranes.

Glycerophospholipids combine with the lipid bilayer comprising a cell membrane. An arrow points to the ionic head and two nonpolar tails of the lipid bilayer.

plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 27: Biomolecules: Lipids
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets a three-dimensional rendering of a lipid bilayer beside the flat structural formula of the molecule that builds it. On the left, a slab of membrane is drawn in perspective with a stepped cutaway at one corner: rows of small green spheres tile the top and bottom faces, and the interior between them is packed with pale tan wavy strands that meet tip to tip along the slab's midplane, so the two leaflets face each other tails inward. On the right, a glycerophospholipid is drawn with a vertical glycerol backbone reading CH2, CH, CH2 from top to bottom. The topmost branch is printed in green and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+, tagged by a green arrow labeled "Ionic head". The two lower branches each run through O-C(=O) into a long tan ribbon of the same shade and waviness as the strands filling the slab, and a magenta label "Nonpolar tails" sends two arrows to their free ends. Matching the green and tan across the two halves lets the reader place each region of the drawn molecule at its position in the assembled sheet. The pairing accounts for how a long nonpolar tail bound to a polar ionic head drives aggregation into a bilayer that keeps hydrocarbon away from water.

elements: LEFT slab: top-leaflet grid of green ionic-head spheres tiling the upper face
LEFT slab: bottom-leaflet grid of green ionic-head spheres tiling the lower face
LEFT slab: upper-leaflet pale-tan wavy tail strands hanging downward from the top heads
LEFT slab: lower-leaflet pale-tan wavy tail strands rising upward from the bottom heads
LEFT slab: midplane seam where the two tail sets meet tip-to-tip
LEFT slab: stepped cutaway notch at the front-top-left corner exposing the interior strands
LEFT slab: pale pink-tan membrane body side faces
RIGHT molecule: vertical glycerol backbone line with stacked labels CH2 (top), CH (middle), CH2 (bottom)
RIGHT molecule: top green branch CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+ with double-bonded O and O- on phosphorus
RIGHT molecule: green arrow and 'Ionic head' text label pointing at the phosphate-choline group
RIGHT molecule: two ester linkages O-C(=O) branching from CH and bottom CH2
RIGHT molecule: two long pale-tan wavy ribbon tails extending rightward from the esters
RIGHT molecule: magenta 'Nonpolar tails' text with two arrows to the free ends of the ribbons
RIGHT molecule: glycerol-linker region (backbone + ester oxygens) as a distinct highlightable zone

interactions.label: Highlight region
interactions.teaches: Selecting a region (by stepping the buttons or clicking the matching spheres / backbone / strands in the scene) glows that part in BOTH the structural formula and the bilayer slab, so the learner sees exactly where the polar head, the linker, and the hydrophobic tails sit inside the assembled membrane

interactions.label: Mapping view
interactions.teaches: Switches which half carries the named callout labels while the matching region glows on the other half, reinforcing the one-to-one correspondence between a single glycerophospholipid's zones and its position in the bilayer

interactions.label: Cutaway depth
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the slice plane through the slab peels away successive layers — first the outer green heads, then the tan tails, finally revealing the midplane tail-to-tail contact — making the outside-polar / inside-nonpolar organization across the membrane thickness directly visible

demo_steps.title: Ionic head maps to the surfaces
demo_steps.narration: With the molecule in focus, the green phosphate-choline head is highlighted; the same green glow appears on the sphere layers capping both faces of the slab, showing the polar heads face the aqueous exterior.

demo_steps.title: Nonpolar tails map to the core
demo_steps.narration: Selecting the tan tails highlights the two wavy ribbons in the formula and the strand-packed interior of the slab, showing the hydrophobic chains are buried away from water.

demo_steps.title: Read the mapping from the assembly
demo_steps.narration: Switching to Assembly view puts the named labels on the slab while the glycerol-linker zone glows in the formula, confirming the ester/backbone band sits at the head-tail interface.

demo_steps.title: Slice to the midplane
demo_steps.narration: Pushing the cutaway to full depth removes the near leaflet's heads and tails, exposing the seam where the two tail sets meet tip-to-tip at the membrane midplane.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Two side-by-side groups. LEFT bilayer slab centered near world x=-3: overall ~4 (X, screen-right width) x 2 (Y, thickness) x 2.5 (Z, receding depth). Top-leaflet head spheres at y=+1, bottom at y=-1, sphere radius ~0.13, arranged ~8 columns (X) x 5 rows (Z) per face as an InstancedMesh. Tan tail strands are wavy tubes/lines spanning y from +/-1 toward the y=0 midplane where the two leaflets meet tip-to-tip. A stepped cutaway notch (~1.5 X x 1 Y x 1.2 Z) is removed from the front-top-left corner to expose interior strands. Membrane body side faces pale pink-tan #d8b3a3. RIGHT molecule on a camera-facing flat group centered near world x=+3.5: vertical glycerol backbone at local x=0 from y=+1.2 (top CH2) through y=0 (CH) to y=-1.2 (bottom CH2); top green branch (#159e7c) runs +X as CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+; two ester O-C(=O) groups at y=0 and y=-1.2 each feed a long tan (#cf9f8a) wavy ribbon extending +X to ~+2.2; green 'Ionic head' arrow/label above the phosphate, magenta (#d6338f) 'Nonpolar tails' label with two arrows at the ribbon free ends. Head spheres green #3ec9a7. Highlight = emissive/opacity boost on the selected group plus dimming of the other two; the same region id drives both halves.
interactionPlan.notes: Three.js: render head spheres as an InstancedMesh for performance; render tails as TubeGeometry along a sine-perturbed path (or fat lines) so they read as wavy strands. Build the structural formula from Line segments plus canvas-texture text sprites on a group that is oriented to face the camera (billboarded) so the formula stays legible at the fixed three-quarter view. Implement the cutaway slider by hiding head-sphere instances and tail tubes whose Z (or distance from the near face) falls within the sliced band, and clip the membrane body with a THREE.Plane clipping plane at the slice position; at depth=1 also reveal the midplane seam line. Wire a raycaster so clicking a sphere / backbone segment / strand sets the highlightRegion state, keeping the click gesture and the explicit stepper in sync. No orbit control — camera is fixed so the flat formula plane is never skewed.
